what_it_does: A trusted execution environment (TEE) is a walled-off secure area inside a processor where sensitive code and data can run in isolation — even the operating system or a cloud provider cannot see inside it. This paper describes ZION, a TEE design for virtual machines (fully isolated software computers running inside a larger physical machine) on RISC-V processors — an open-source chip instruction set gaining traction in data centers and embedded devices. Existing RISC-V TEE designs either work only at the level of individual programs (not full virtual machines) or require special custom hardware extensions unavailable on most real chips. ZION works on ordinary, commodity RISC-V hardware by cleverly combining two standard RISC-V memory protection features: physical memory protection (PMP, which marks address ranges as off-limits) and regular page-table-based virtual memory (which maps virtual addresses to physical ones). It also introduces a fast path for switching between the secure virtual machine and the host, and a method for securely sharing specific memory pages with virtualized device drivers. Based on the abstract, the main contribution is achieving strong isolation on unmodified hardware.
